skill.description: Processes Markdown article link lists, fetches page text, and drafts rewritten posts with an AI writing workflow.
skill.summary: Turn Markdown article links into fetched, rewritten draft posts.
skill.author: wangdefou-dev

security_audit.summary: I found no evidence of obfuscated malware or deliberate credential exfiltration. Confirmed risks include project .env and API key access, unrestricted outbound URL fetching, automatic file watching and reads, and an npm script execution path.

remediation.suggestion: Allow only approved public hosts, reject localhost and private IP ranges, and require user confirmation for new domains.
Use a scoped secret provider when possible, avoid loading the whole project .env, and restrict custom API base URLs.
Remove automatic npm execution or require explicit confirmation before running skill:verify. Avoid shell execution for fixed commands.
Delimit fetched content as untrusted source text and instruct the model not to follow instructions found inside articles.
Remove EVALUATION.json from the published skill package so marketplace review is based on source behavior, not bundled claims.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: EVALUATION.json includes self-assessment fields that claim safe_to_publish is true and summarize the skill as low risk. This embedded self-approval can bias automated review and should not be trusted as authority.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file does not directly command the auditor to skip review, but it asserts its own safety in machine-readable audit fields. The prompt-injection guidance flags self-approval claims as suspicious.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Article Content Enters LLM Prompt
semantic_findings.description: Fetched article titles and body text are inserted directly into the model prompt. A malicious page can include instructions that alter generated output or weaken safety requirements.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The prompt template directly interpolates articleTitle and articleContent into the user message. There is no visible instruction boundary telling the model to treat fetched content as untrusted data.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted URL Fetching From Markdown Input
semantic_findings.description: Any parsed link that starts with http is fetched without host validation, scheme restrictions beyond the prefix, or private-network blocking. An untrusted input list can make the runner contact internal or unwanted endpoints.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The parser accepts any link beginning with http, and fetchArticleContent passes that URL directly to fetch. I found no allowlist, DNS/IP filtering, or localhost/private address guard.

content.user_title: Process Article Lists Into Draft Posts
content.value_statement: Collecting many article links creates slow copying and rewriting work. This skill watches a Markdown list, fetches articles, and drafts rewritten posts.
actual_capabilities: Parses Markdown files for article titles and HTTP links.
Watches a local input folder for new Markdown or text files.
Fetches article pages and extracts readable body text.
Generates rewritten draft posts with an Anthropic model.
Writes generated Markdown files with source metadata.
Moves processed input files into an archive folder.
limitations: Requires an Anthropic API key unless mock mode is enabled.
Cannot fetch pages that block bots or require login.
Generated drafts require human review before publishing.
Untrusted links can expose the runner to unwanted network requests.

best_practices: Use only public article URLs that you are allowed to fetch.
Run mock mode first to confirm the input file format.
Review every generated draft for accuracy, attribution, and policy compliance.
anti_patterns: Do not process private, login-only, or confidential links.
Do not publish generated text without human review.
Do not run the watcher in a project with unrelated sensitive input files.

faq.question: What input format does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects Markdown or text files containing article links in title and URL format.

faq.question: Where are generated drafts saved?
faq.answer: Drafts are written under the configured project output folder for Defou Stanley posts.

faq.question: Does it need network access?
faq.answer: Yes. It fetches article pages and sends prompts to the configured Anthropic API endpoint.

faq.question: Can it run without an API key?
faq.answer: Mock mode can test the file workflow, but real generation requires an Anthropic API key.

faq.question: Does it change input files?
faq.answer: Yes. After processing, it moves each input list into an archive folder.

faq.question: Is the generated content ready to publish?
faq.answer: No. The output is a draft and should be reviewed for accuracy, originality, and permissions.
